description: Shared base preset: Renovate's best practices, one Monday-morning window in Europe/Paris, a 3-day soak on every release, minors, patches and digests in one weekly pull request, prek.toml hook revs, labels by kind, and majors of data-owning images held for approval. Extend it with `github>KevinDeBenedetti/renovate-config` and keep only the repository's own rules next to it.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes skip the schedule and the minimum release age (Renovate's own behaviour), and stand out in the PR list.

customManagers.description: prek hook revs. Renovate has no prek manager (the pre-commit one reads .pre-commit-config.yaml only), so each `rev = "…"` in prek.toml carries a `# renovate: datasource=<datasource> depName=<depName>` comment on the line above. Two forms: a tag (`rev = "v1.2.3"`), or a commit frozen to its tag (`rev = "<40-hex sha>"  # frozen: v1.2.3`, what `prek update --freeze` writes), whose commit and comment move together. The tag form needs a non-hex character, so a frozen commit is never read as a tag. Any prek.toml outside ignorePaths: config:best-practices ignores `**/examples/**`, so a repository that wants examples/prek.toml read sets its own ignorePaths.

packageRules.description: Soak every release for 3 days before proposing it, whatever the ecosystem (config:best-practices only does it for npm): a release pulled within days (broken, or a compromised publish) never reaches a PR. internalChecksFilter is `strict` by default, so no PR opens until a version is old enough; pending ones show on the Dependency Dashboard. Security updates do not wait.

Update types that carry no release timestamp of their own: with the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour (timestamp-required) the soak above would hold them forever. Same exceptions as Renovate's security:minimumReleaseAge* presets, for every datasource.

KevinDeBenedetti repositories only: their KevinDeBenedetti/github-workflows pins (workflows, prek.toml) move with each of its releases, through the pull request its propagate-release job opens, so Renovate would only duplicate it, and would re-pin it. Any other repository that extends this preset gets Renovate's updates of those pins as usual.

GitHub Actions bumps are CI changes: `ci(deps)` rather than `chore(deps)`, so they stay out of the release notes. Only majors keep it: minors, patches and digests join the non-major group below, which sets its own type.
prek hook bumps are tooling: `chore(deps)` and their own label.
A major gets its own label so it stands out in the PR list and the notifications, instead of being merged as a routine bump.
A major of an image that owns data is a migration, not a bump: no PR until it is approved on the Dependency Dashboard, and never automerged. Minors, patches and digests flow as usual.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ This image owns data. A new major may refuse the files the current one wrote: read its upgrade notes, plan the migration (dump and restore, or the project's own upgrade path) and take a backup first. Merging alone can take the database down.

packageRules.description: Minors, patches and digests in one weekly pull request (branch renovate/all-minor-patch), instead of one per package each running the full CI; majors stay one each (:separateMultipleMajorReleases). An explicit rule rather than group:allNonMajor, which leaves digest and pinDigest out, and config:best-practices pins every Docker image and GitHub Action by digest. Last, after the soak rules: grouping changes no minimumReleaseAge, so each update still waits its 3 days. A repository's own groupName rules come after the preset's and keep their own pull request; a package that must stay alone (a checksum pinned next to it, say) sets `"groupName": null`. One failing update holds the whole group: exclude it from the Dependency Dashboard. Always `chore(deps)`: the group mixes ecosystems, so the GitHub Actions rule's `ci` would otherwise hide runtime bumps from the release notes whenever an action came first.
